title: [Audit] 🚨 Security & Anomalies
description: Mean-severity risk scoring, privileged operations, failures and newly seen identities.

config.description: Average severity weight across scoring events, on the same 0–50 scale as the weights: config change 50, key invalidation 45, failure 40, anonymous denial 35, destructive change 30, other Kibana change 25, workflow execution 10. Executions weigh least on purpose — they are the one class with unbounded cadence, and a scheduled workflow firing every minute would otherwise turn total risk back into an event count. Routine activity scores 0 and is excluded, so this is not a disguised event count — read it with Scoring events beside it.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change IS NOT NULL OR attributes.event.outcome == "failure" OR attributes.event.action IN ("invalidate_apikeys","anonymous_access_denied") OR (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))) | STATS n = COUNT(*) BY attributes.event.action, scc = attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change IS NOT NULL, attributes.event.outcome, resource.attributes.service.name, et = MV_CONCAT(attributes.event.type, ","), housekeeping = (attributes.event.action IS NOT NULL AND attributes.event.action == "invalidate_apikeys" AND attributes.user.name IS NOT NULL AND attributes.user.name IN ("elastic.maintenance","autoscaling","elasticsearch-controller","elastic/fleet-server","elastic/kibana") AND attributes.api_key.name IS NULL) | EVAL attributes.event.type = SPLIT(et, ","), attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change = CASE(scc, "present") | EVAL risk = CASE(housekeeping, 0, attributes.event.action == "invalidate_apikeys", 45, attributes.event.action == "anonymous_access_denied", 35, attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change IS NOT NULL, 50, attributes.event.outcome == "failure", 40, (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))) AND attributes.event.action IN ("workflow_run","workflow_test","workflow_execution_cancel"), 10, (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))) AND (attributes.event.type == "deletion" OR attributes.event.action == "rule_disable"), 30, (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))), 25, 0) | WHERE risk > 0 | STATS risk_total = SUM(risk * n), scoring_events = SUM(n) | EVAL mean_severity = ROUND(1.0 * risk_total / scoring_events, 1) | EVAL `Mean severity (of 50)` = mean_severity | KEEP `Mean severity (of 50)`

config.description: Security configuration changes recorded by Elasticsearch (API keys created, changed or invalidated, roles and user profiles written) — the total that the Config changes table and the event feed below draw from. Kibana's own API-key clean-up (invalidate_apikeys by the elastic/kibana service account through no named key, every few seconds) is left out, as on Command Center's Privileged ops; the second line says how many such events the range held. The range ends a minute ago, so nothing in it is still arriving; each panel reads the clock for itself, up to a second apart, so two panels side by side can differ by the events of that second at either end of the range: usually none, a few on a busy all-traffic count or during a burst.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change IS NOT NULL | EVAL housekeeping = (attributes.event.action IS NOT NULL AND attributes.event.action == "invalidate_apikeys" AND attributes.user.name IS NOT NULL AND attributes.user.name IN ("elastic.maintenance","autoscaling","elasticsearch-controller","elastic/fleet-server","elastic/kibana") AND attributes.api_key.name IS NULL) | STATS `Config changes` = COUNT(*) WHERE NOT housekeeping, cleanups = COUNT(*) WHERE housekeeping | EVAL housekeeping_note = CASE(cleanups == 0, "no cleanups in range", CONCAT("excl. ", CASE(LENGTH(TO_STRING(cleanups)) <= 3, TO_STRING(cleanups), LENGTH(TO_STRING(cleanups)) <= 6, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(cleanups), LENGTH(TO_STRING(cleanups)) - 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(cleanups), 3)), LENGTH(TO_STRING(cleanups)) <= 9, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(cleanups), LENGTH(TO_STRING(cleanups)) - 6), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(cleanups), LENGTH(TO_STRING(cleanups)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(cleanups), 3)), CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(cleanups), LENGTH(TO_STRING(cleanups)) - 9), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(cleanups), LENGTH(TO_STRING(cleanups)) - 8, 3), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(cleanups), LENGTH(TO_STRING(cleanups)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(cleanups), 3))), " cleanups"))

config.description: invalidate_apikeys requests in range (one request can name several keys) — legitimate rotation, or a credential being revoked in a hurry; a subset of Config changes. Kibana's own API-key clean-up (invalidate_apikeys by the elastic/kibana service account through no named key, every few seconds) is left out, as on Command Center's Privileged ops; the second line says how many such events the range held. Risk scoring leaves the same clean-up out (it scores 0), so the invalidations it weighs are these.

config.description: Events with a failure outcome: failed sign-ins (authentication_failed or anonymous_access_denied, one per request; the realm_authentication_failed events Elasticsearch writes for each realm an attempt tried are left out, so an attempt counts once), denials and any other failed action. Counted as on Identity & Access's Failed or denied tile, so the two agree.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.event.action IN ("authentication_failed","anonymous_access_denied") OR (attributes.event.outcome == "failure" AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR attributes.event.action != "realm_authentication_failed")) | STATS `Failures` = COUNT(*)

FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.event.action == "anonymous_access_denied" | STATS `Anonymous denials` = COUNT(*)

config.title: 🚨 Config changes by identity and action · newest 9 at most (empty when none in range)
config.description: Security configuration changes grouped by identity and action, the most recently active first; in a busy range the quieter pairs are beyond the rows shown, so Events here add up to the Config changes tile only when every pair fits. Kibana's own API-key clean-up (invalidate_apikeys by the elastic/kibana service account through no named key, every few seconds) is left out, as on Command Center's Privileged ops. Latest target is what the newest of those changes named (the API key, the key ids of an invalidation, the role, or the user profile), and Targets counts the different ones named across all of them: hundreds of invalidations over hundreds of keys is rotation, hundreds over one key is a loop. A profile activation names no target (it is the signed-in user's own profile), so it reads "(none named in the payload)" and 0. A key named "TaskManager: … - <id>" is one Kibana created to run a task on that identity's behalf: the id at its end is its owner's, not a name for it. The full JSON payload of every change is in the Config-change event feed at the foot of the page. An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email. Often empty over the default hour on a healthy project; widen the time range to see older rows.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change IS NOT NULL AND NOT (attributes.event.action IS NOT NULL AND attributes.event.action == "invalidate_apikeys" AND attributes.user.name IS NOT NULL AND attributes.user.name IN ("elastic.maintenance","autoscaling","elasticsearch-controller","elastic/fleet-server","elastic/kibana") AND attributes.api_key.name IS NULL) | GROK attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change """"name":"%{DATA:t_name}"""" | GROK attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change """"ids":\[%{DATA:t_ids}\]""" | GROK attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change """"id":"%{DATA:t_id}"""" | GROK attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change """"uid":"%{DATA:t_uid}"""" | EVAL target = COALESCE(t_name, REPLACE(t_ids, "\"", ""), t_id, t_uid) | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>") | STATS events = COUNT(*), targets = COUNT_DISTINCT(SPLIT(target, ",")), latest = LAST(target, @timestamp), last_change = MAX(@timestamp) BY actor, action = attributes.event.action | SORT last_change DESC | EVAL actor_scope = CASE(actor IN ("elastic.maintenance","autoscaling","elasticsearch-controller","elastic/fleet-server","elastic/kibana"), "platform", actor IN ("<anonymous>","<unauthenticated-cloud-access-token>","<unauthenticated-saml-user>","<unauthenticated-cloud-api-key>"), "unauthenticated", "tenant") | EVAL latest = REPLACE(latest, ",", ", ") | EVAL latest = CASE(LENGTH(latest) > 72, CONCAT(LEFT(latest, 71), "…"), latest) | EVAL latest = COALESCE(latest, "(none named in the payload)") | LIMIT 9 | EVAL actor = CASE((LENGTH(actor) == 20 AND actor RLIKE "[-_A-Za-z0-9]{20}" AND NOT actor RLIKE "[0-9]{20}"), CONCAT(LEFT(actor, 5), "… · Cloud API key"), actor)

config.title: Highest-severity actions, by how rare
config.description: The highest-severity scoring actions in range, one row per action and weight, placed by how often each happened: rarer is further left, so the top-left is rare and high-severity — look there first. Shows the top 12 by severity, rarest first within a weight; the subtitle says how many actions scored in all. On a quiet range the top 12 reach down to routine Kibana changes (weight 25), which can be frequent: rare is a position on this chart, not a filter. Each row ends with its severity weight, which the colour repeats: one colour per weight, blue for 10 up to deep red for 50, keyed below the chart. A failed change scores 40 whatever it changed, so it gets its own row, marked (failed). Hover a point for how many identities did it and when. Routine activity scores 0 and is not shown. Kibana's own API-key clean-up scores 0, as it is left out of the Key invalidations tile, so invalidate_apikeys here counts the same invalidations that tile does.

config.title: Risk over time
config.description: Summed severity weight per interval, routine activity excluded, split by who it came from: tenant identities, Elastic platform automation, or unauthenticated requests. Spikes are clusters of privileged, failed or denied activity. The axis always spans the whole range: a blank stretch means nothing scored then, or, on a project younger than the range, that the audit stream had not started yet.

config.title: Identities by first appearance in range · newest 8 at most
config.description: Identities ordered by their first event inside the selected range, latest first, from signal events only (query internals are left out, as on every gated panel). First seen is within the range, not ever: an identity that was already active when the range opened also shows a first-seen near its start. New reads "no" for those (first seen in the opening twelfth of the range) and "yes" otherwise; on a project whose audit history is shorter than the range, every identity reads "yes". A "yes" near the top is an identity worth a question; widen the range to tell a new identity from a returning one. Client IPs is 0 for identities whose events record no client address (the Kibana service account, platform automation). An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IS NULL OR NOT "cluster:admin/xpack/security/api_key/get", "cluster:admin/xpack/security/api_key/query"))) AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>") | STATS first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp), events = COUNT(*), ips = CASE(TO_LONG(first_seen) - TO_LONG(TO_DATETIME(?_tstart)) > (TO_LONG(TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) - TO_LONG(TO_DATETIME(?_tstart))) / 12, "yes", "no") | LIMIT 8 | EVAL actor = CASE((LENGTH(actor) == 20 AND actor RLIKE "[-_A-Za-z0-9]{20}" AND NOT actor RLIKE "[0-9]{20}"), CONCAT(LEFT(actor, 5), "… · Cloud API key"), actor)

config.title: Risk leaderboard — top identities by total severity · 10 at most
config.description: Identities ranked by total accumulated severity, so sustained behaviour outranks a single high-severity event; only the top of the ranking fits the panel. Scope separates tenant identities from Elastic platform automation and unauthenticated requests — without it elastic.maintenance can top this table, because Elastic platform automation performs routine security config changes itself. Privileged counts the identity's security config changes the way the Config changes tile does. Kibana's own API-key clean-up is left out of both columns: it scores 0, so the elastic/kibana service account appears here only for something else it did. Identity is the email for a person and the key name for a named API key. To follow one person, pick them in the Person (email) control; the pin carries to Actor 360. An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email.

config.title: Why these identities scored — top risky actions, with their weight · 10 at most
config.description: The receipts behind the leaderboard: the identity and action pairs that contributed the most risk, with what each action weighed, how many times it happened, and when it last did. Risk total is weight × events, the same quantity the leaderboard sums. Only the largest contributions fit the panel, so a rare action can be missing here: Highest-severity actions, by how rare lists the actions by severity instead. To follow one person, pick them in the Person (email) control; the pin carries to Actor 360. An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email.

config.title: Top failures and denials by identity and action · 8 at most (empty = good)
config.description: Failed and denied operations, one row per identity and action, the most frequent first; only the top rows fit the panel. These are the events the Failures tile counts (every denial and failed sign-in carries a failure outcome), and the Anonymous denials tile is their anonymous_access_denied rows. A failure is scored on a row of its own in Why these identities scored, so where a pair appears in both, Events is the same number. Latest IP is the client address of the newest of those events and Client IPs counts the different addresses they came from: many addresses behind one identity is a spray, one address behind many identities is one source trying names. An address tagged (internal) is the platform-internal hop (100.64/10), as on Geo & Network: the platform calling on the client's behalf, not the client, and Client IPs counts it too. Scope separates unauthenticated probes from tenant identities and Elastic platform automation. API keys and native users (elastic, admin) carry no email, so an Identity that is not an email does not mean an external probe — read Scope. To follow one person, pick them in the Person (email) control; the pin carries to Actor 360. An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email. An empty panel means nothing matched in the time range, which is the healthy state; any row here is worth reading.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.event.action IN ("authentication_failed","anonymous_access_denied") OR (attributes.event.outcome == "failure" AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR attributes.event.action != "realm_authentication_failed")) | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>") | STATS events = COUNT(*), ips = COUNT_DISTINCT(client.ip), ip = LAST(client.ip, @timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY actor, action = attributes.event.action | SORT events DESC | EVAL actor_scope = CASE(actor IN ("elastic.maintenance","autoscaling","elasticsearch-controller","elastic/fleet-server","elastic/kibana"), "platform", actor IN ("<anonymous>","<unauthenticated-cloud-access-token>","<unauthenticated-saml-user>","<unauthenticated-cloud-api-key>"), "unauthenticated", "tenant") | EVAL ip = CASE(CIDR_MATCH(ip, "100.64.0.0/10"), CONCAT(TO_STRING(ip), " (internal)"), TO_STRING(ip)) | LIMIT 8 | EVAL actor = CASE((LENGTH(actor) == 20 AND actor RLIKE "[-_A-Za-z0-9]{20}" AND NOT actor RLIKE "[0-9]{20}"), CONCAT(LEFT(actor, 5), "… · Cloud API key"), actor)

config.title: Config-change event feed · newest 1,000 at most (empty when none in range)
config.description: Every security configuration change the Config changes tile counts, as its own event, newest first, with the payload in full over two lines; expand a row to read a longer one. Kibana's own API-key clean-up (invalidate_apikeys by the elastic/kibana service account through no named key, every few seconds) is left out, as on Command Center's Privileged ops. Discover returns at most the newest 1,000 events, and its result count is that cap rather than the total: when it reads 1,000, the Config changes tile at the top has the total. Scroll the grid for older rows. An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email. Often empty over the default hour on a healthy project; widen the time range to see older rows.

config.title: Mutation feed · newest 1,000 at most
config.description: Creates, updates and deletes across Kibana and Elasticsearch security config, newest first. Object is what the change named: the saved object or feature object for a Kibana change; for an Elasticsearch security change, the API key's name, the key ids of an invalidation, the role or the profile, with its full JSON payload under Message. Kibana's own API-key clean-up (invalidate_apikeys by the elastic/kibana service account through no named key, every few seconds) is left out, as on Command Center's Privileged ops. Space id is the space's id, the /s/<id> in its URL: the audit stream records no space display name, not even on a space read. It is empty on an Elasticsearch security change, which belongs to no space. Spaces that tooling creates and deletes (review or test spaces) are real activity, and so is the config object Kibana creates the first time a space is opened. Discover returns at most the newest 1,000 events, and its result count is that cap rather than the total. Scroll the grid for older rows; to reach older events still, narrow the time range. An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email.
